claim: Coolify preview deployments are disabled by default; once enabled, every PR opened against the configured branch auto-deploys to a unique URL, and the GitHub App method is recommended because it posts automated status comments on the PR.
quote: Preview deployments are automatically deleted once the associated pull request is merged or closed, ensuring a clean environment.

claim: The preview URL template supports {{pr_id}} (PR number as subdomain) and {{random}} (unique random subdomain); production env vars are isolated and never exposed to PR-triggered previews, which use their own variable set.
quote: {{pr_id}}: Uses the pull request ID as the subdomain ... {{random}}: Generates a unique random subdomain ... never exposed to preview deployments triggered from pull requests

claim: By default only repository members/collaborators/contributors can trigger PR deployments (public PR deployments are an opt-in), and previews are not retroactively applied to PRs opened before the feature was enabled.
quote: Preview deployments aren't retroactively applied to PRs opened before the feature was enabled—you must manually deploy these using the dashboard.

claim: A real user set up Coolify PR previews by creating a private GitHub App through Coolify (auto-collecting App ID, Installation ID, Client ID/Secret, Webhook Secret) requesting read access to administration/code plus read/write on pull requests for commenting, and a Cloudflare wildcard '*' A record to the server IP.
quote: requested read access to administration and code, plus read/write access to pull requests for commenting on PRs ... creating an "A" record in Cloudflare with hostname "*" pointing to the server IP

claim: The default {{pr_id}}.{{domain}} template produced a multi-level hostname (e.g. 6-conversus.billyle.dev) that triggered an SSL error against a single-level wildcard cert; the user fixed it by switching to {{pr_id}}-{{domain}}.
quote: encountered an SSL error when using the default template {{pr_id}}.{{domain}} format ... They resolved this by modifying the template to {{pr_id}}-{{domain}}

claim: Coolify has no upper limit, TTL, or auto-expiration for preview deployments; the 'Max Concurrent Builds' setting only caps build parallelism, so accumulating previews can exhaust RAM/CPU and degrade production on constrained homelab servers (repo at 56.6k stars).
quote: every PR opened against the configured branch creates a preview deployment with no limit ... The existing "Max Concurrent Builds" server setting only limits build parallelism, not running environments ... No TTL or auto-expiration mechanism exists

claim: Coolify isolates preview containers via {uuid}-pr-{id} naming and prioritizes preview-specific env vars when pull_request_id !== 0; GitLab is supported through a parallel webhook controller, but the database isolation strategy is undocumented and lifecycle management is manual.
quote: When a deployment is identified as a preview (pull_request_id !== 0), the system prioritizes or includes preview-specific environment variables ... GitLab is explicitly supported ... database isolation strategy and resource scaling limits are unspecified

claim: For Docker Compose multi-service apps, Coolify rewrites container names per preview (e.g. db-pr-295, frontend-pr-295), which breaks hardcoded service references in nginx upstreams and DB connections; workarounds involve a separate DB instance plus env vars or the COOLIFY_BRANCH variable.
quote: the docker compose file that is generated changes the container names (db-pr-295, frontend-pr-295 etc.). This breaks the connection to the database, and nginx config, as it relies on the original container names.

claim: Versus managed cloud preview platforms, Coolify requires custom configuration for per-preview database provisioning (no automatic database forking) and lacks automated teardown scheduling / idle-detection cleanup.
quote: Coolify and Fly.io require custom configuration for database provisioning in preview environments ... Coolify lacks "automated teardown scheduling"—a feature Northflank includes for idle detection and schedule-based cleanup.
